canary_flow_trace_findings.observation: no 'darkfac-canary' entry existed in .factory/projects.json; the first worker job (grill) for any canary-submitted run would fail with UnknownProjectError
service was behind profiles: ["canary"] with restart: "no" (one-shot); nothing in the repo scheduled it, so it never ran unattended
canary_flow_trace_findings.status: fixed_in_this_closeout: run_loop + --every-seconds 3600, profiles removed, restart: unless-stopped

canary_flow_trace_findings.source: core/line/workspace.py:117 (reads GITHUB_TOKEN), deploy/dokploy/docker-compose.cloud.yml darkfac-worker (before this closeout)
canary_flow_trace_findings.observation: the worker container declared no GITHUB_TOKEN at all (only GITHUB_PAT existed, in env.cloud.example, used only by the unrelated hub compose's build context); a private repo like darkfac-canary would fail HTTPS clone/push with no auth
canary_flow_trace_findings.status: fixed_in_this_closeout: GITHUB_TOKEN=${GITHUB_TOKEN:-} added to darkfac-worker; the real value must still be provisioned in the Dokploy vault (external, out of scope)

canary_flow_trace_findings.observation: none of DOKPLOY_API_URL/DOKPLOY_API_KEY/DOKPLOY_DEPLOY_URL were wired into docker-compose.cloud.yml for any project; without at least one, DokployDeploymentAdapter.start() silently no-ops (no transport, no webhook) and reconcile() never leaves IN_PROGRESS -- build_deploy would hang for every project, not just the canary
canary_flow_trace_findings.status: fixed_in_this_closeout: env passthroughs added to darkfac-worker; real values (incl. the canary's own Dokploy application id KCTz2USVQhNp_R6BuTxh1, already set as darkfac-canary's deploy.params.service_name) must still be provisioned externally

canary_flow_trace_findings.observation: checked whether a volume mount shadows /app/.factory and hides projects.json inside the container -- it does not: only /app/.factory/artifacts, /app/.factory/test_logs and (for the canary service) /app/.factory/reports/canary are volume-mounted as subdirectories; .factory/projects.json at the root is baked into the image at build time and stays visible as long as the image is rebuilt after this PR merges
canary_flow_trace_findings.status: checked; not a blocker, contrary to the hypothesis in the task brief

canary_flow_trace_findings.observation: the canary submits its demand by writing directly to the shared ControlStore (Postgres iff DARKFAC_HF02_DATABASE_URL is set), not through the coordinator's authenticated HTTP /api/v1/tasks route -- so DARKFAC_ALLOWED_PROJECT_ID (which only gates the HTTP route) never blocks the canary's own submission path

the canary's demand text is deliberately deterministic and unambiguous, but grill is a live LLM call each day and its ambiguity judgment is not guaranteed deterministic -- a day where grill pauses for clarification would break the green streak that day
canary_flow_trace_findings.status: inherent design risk, not a code bug; not fixed (would require changing grill's own judgment logic, out of this closeout's scope) -- monitor via the canary's own outcome=in_progress/failed reports

canary_flow_trace_findings.observation: development/planning/review stages need a worker with harness:claude or harness:codex capabilities published, which requires a one-time interactive OAuth/device-code login on the VPS -- already a known, documented human-only item, unrelated to the canary specifically
canary_flow_trace_findings.status: known pre-existing external blocker; out of scope, not re-verified in this session
